name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: Nuclear risk was on the agenda of the Trump–Xi–Putin Shenzhen summit; no arms-control treaty or talks timetable found
state: Trump, Xi and Putin discussed nuclear arms at their summit in Shenzhen in the week of 17 Nov (Hurriyet Daily News), but commentators noted no binding pact was in prospect (Modern Diplomacy, 18 Nov). US–Russia treaty limits have been absent since New START expired in February. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use was found as of 21 Nov, so Watch holds on the arms-control lapse.
for_you: No direct effect. The absence of arms-control limits raises long-run risk rather than immediate danger.

sources.title: Hurriyet Daily News — Trump to discuss nuclear arms, wars with Putin and Xi

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
